- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model often overshoots downward; reduce forecast slope or add a small upward bias to prevent premature correction.  
- If sentiment turns positive after a downtrend, model frequently underreacts; increase forecast slope or add a small upward bias to capture sentiment-driven rebound.  
- Model tends to underestimate true price in early part of 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile; apply a small upward bias to first 5–7 days of forecast.  
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model often underestimates true price; apply a small upward bias to avoid missing upward momentum.  
- Model frequently overestimates price in the final 5–7 days of 30-day forecast; reduce forecast slope or apply downward bias to avoid overcorrection near end of horizon.  
- If sentiment shows strong negative momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative values), model tends to overreact; reduce forecast magnitude or add smoothing to avoid extreme sell-off.  
- Model often fails to capture mean reversion in medium-term (10–20 day) horizon; adjust forecast to align with recent 10-day average if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.
